11b) You are praised as the Lord, the power of resonance (*nāda*), radiant, having the nature of light, and whose own form is the syllable *A*.

You are Śiva’s eldest [consort], Vāmā, Raudrī, and Manonmanī; you are the form of the Bindu, the Daughter-in-law (*vadhūtā*), the Half-moon (*ardhacandra*), and the Triangle (*trikoṇa*). You are the syllables *A*, *U*, *Ma*, *Ī*, and *Sa*; you are the single unity of the luminous.
You do not undergo transformation; you abide in the form of Bhaga, possessing the primordial nature of forbearance (*kṣāntatva*),
the source of existence, the mother of Rudra who is invoked as Śrīkaṇṭha,

and likewise the infinite power, the very subtle one, she who honors the three forms, she whose essence consists of the lunar days (*tithi*), she who has become Sthāṇu, and she who is the eye of Hara.

O Bhairavī, you who are worshipped through the grace of the essence of Ṛṃ Thiśa and Bhautīśa; you who are the consort of Kula, Śaṅkara, and Mahāsena; you who extend to the end of the sixteen; you who are the source of the mass of nectar-drops; you who have leaped over the body in the *Spanda*; you who bestow the supreme bliss of liberation upon all those who are well-composed.

O Goddess, O Beloved of Mahālakṣmī, that pure human being who always remembers [the names] four, five, six, seven, or eight times— even he, though stained by the great sins of stealing gold, violating another’s wife, killing a Brahmin, or killing a cow, becomes free from fear of thieves, fire, weapons, the ocean, or even the mountain peak, due to his affection for Your son.
